title: TCALL - DigiTrans -Digitalization and transfer of technical innovations in Long Term Care
summary:
In Germany, over five million people depend on care services, and this number could rise to eight million by 2050 due to demographic changes. Ensuring adequate care for everyone is already a significant challenge. Digital care technologies could offer support but remain underutilized. 

Studies suggest that digital care technologies can ease caregiving and support care staff. This is where the DigiTrans project comes in. The initiative aims to test and implement digital care technologies in praxis and establish them in nursing homes over the long term. The project involves selecting, testing, and evaluating digital care technologies in several steps. Successful solutions will then be expanded to other care facilities and regions. Additionally, strategies will be developed to enable sustainable and scalable use of these innovations.

Key steps of the project:
- identifying at least two suitable digital care technologies with input from care staff, residents, and other stakeholders.
- testing and evaluating these digital care technologies in praxis, focusing on usability, acceptance, and effectiveness.
- rolling out successful digital care technologies across participating facilities.
- developing strategies for scaling the technologies to other regions.
- creating training materials to help care staff adopt these digital care technologies.
- spreading findings through publishing in reports and international journals.

Goals:
The project seeks to demonstrate how digital care technologies can make caregiving easier while improving the quality of life for those in need of care. A key priority is ensuring that all stakeholders – care staff, residents, and their families – embrace these changes and benefit from the improvements.

A practical approach:
DigiTrans focuses on testing digital care technologies under real-world conditions in care facilities. The goal is to identify solutions that offer the most significant benefits and are easy to integrate into daily routines. Beyond technical aspects, the project fosters a new culture of collaboration between science, industry, and society.

interventions.name:
Intervention group:
Three nursing homes in Bremen are restructered into academic teaching nursing homes. Over a total period of nine years, various digital care technologies will be implemented, tested and evaluated in order to provide state-of-the-art care.

Control groups:
Each academic nursing home is not only an intervention facility, but also a control facility for the other academic nursing home. The academic nursing home in which a selected digital care technology is implemented is defined as the intervention facility. The remaining two academic

External control groups:
Each academic nursing home is matched with an external control facility that corresponds to the academic nursing home in various aspects such as size, care degree distribution, localisation, staffing, care home costs, etc.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Principally: voluntary participation

- Nursing homes:
Nursing homes in Bremen that have stated their interest, the selection resides with the TCALL initiative.

- Employees: 
Questionnaires and focus groups:  Direct involvement in the nursing care of residents

- Residents:
i) Survey: all residents who are able to complete a questionnaire independently or with support according to the assessment of the nursing staff. For cognitively impaired residents, for example, an external assessment is provided.
ii) Focus groups with residents who, according to the assessment of the care professionals, are cognitively able to do so
Exclusion criteria:
- Residents:
terminal residents, living in the respecting nursing home less than 6 weeks

- Employees:
survey: employment less than 4 weeks.
